newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS-ASDA calls bought ahead of results.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS-ASDA calls bought ahead of results.

text.p: Expectations that British supermarket sector favourite ASDA Group will produce a sparkling set of interim results this week sparked interest in ASDA calls, dealers said on Monday.
They noted a buyer of 1,000 January 130 calls at 2p as the underlying shares rose to a record on heavy trading volume.
ASDA, whose shares were up 1-1/4 to 123p at 1404 GMT, is set to release its half year results on Thursday.
Analysts were forecasting pre-tax profits of 155 million to 161 million stg from 138.3 million stg a year ago, with a dividend payout of 0.85p per share, up from 0.72p previously.
Dealers noted a couple of relatively big volatility trades in Shell Transport calls. They said there were at least two buyers of some 2,400 April 950 calls against stock.
Shares in Shell eased 1p to 984-1/2p. They were among the most actively traded shares in London.
A cautiously bullish trade was seen in General Electric Co options where 500 February 390 calls were bought against the sale of 500 February 360 puts.
The spread, a so-called "split synthetic," will expire worthless if the shares, down 3p to 368p, remain between 360p and 390p.

Dealers also noted a seller of 700 February 1200 calls on British Aerospace, whose shares eased 3p to 1122-1/2. They sank as low as 1111p earlier following news of Boeing Co's proposed takeover of McDonnell Douglas.
Elsewhere, most activity in FTSE 100 index options revolved around the rollover of December contracts, which expire on Friday, into March contracts, dealers said.
The FTSE 100 was up 17.1 points to 3,989.5.
